faq.q: What type of lever is a nutcracker?
faq.a: A second-class lever: the pivot is at the end, the load in the middle and the effort at the far end, so the force is multiplied.
asks: Why does a nutcracker multiply force?

faq.q: What type of lever are tweezers?
faq.a: Tweezers are a third-class lever: the pivot is at one end, your fingers push in the middle, and the tips grip at the far end.
asks: Are tweezers a third class lever?

faq.q: Why do tweezers not grip very hard?
faq.a: Your fingers are closer to the pivot than the tips, so the tips press with less force than you do. In return, a small finger movement opens and closes the tips a lot.
asks: Why are third class levers weaker?

faq.a: Long tongs keep your hand away from heat and let a small movement of your hand open the ends wide, giving reach and control.
asks: Why use tongs instead of fingers?

faq.q: What else is a third-class lever?
faq.a: Fishing rods, brooms, chopsticks, kitchen tongs and your forearm, where the biceps pulls between the elbow and the hand.

facts: In a third-class lever the effort is between the pivot and the load.
Third-class levers always give less force than the effort but more movement.
